steps.say: The Le Fort ladder is climbing the face in three steps, and each step is detaching a bigger block. Le Fort one is floating the tooth-bearing maxilla, Le Fort two is carrying the nose and central face as a pyramid, and Le Fort three is freeing the entire facial skeleton from the skull base. Learning the three lines is reading every midface scan.
steps.tx: **Le Fort fractures** (transverse maxillary fracture lines from high-energy facial impact) climb in **three** levels: **Le Fort I** floats the alveolus and palate, **Le Fort II** carries the central face as a pyramid, and **Le Fort III** frees the whole facial skeleton from the cranial base. Each higher line detaches a larger block, so naming the level predicts instability and the fixation plan.

vis.alt: Skull diagram showing Le Fort one two and three fracture lines with an orbital blowout panel.
vis.caption: Le Fort I, II, and III lines with an orbital floor blowout; all three break the pterygoid plates. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The lowest line is cutting across above the tooth roots. The Guerin fracture is separating the alveolar process and palate from the midface skeleton while everything above is staying put. A mobile upper jaw with malocclusion is announcing this low transverse pattern.
steps.tx: **Le Fort I fracture** (the **Guerin** transverse maxillary split) separates the **alveolar process** (the tooth-bearing ridge) and palate from the midface skeleton above the **dental roots** (the tooth sockets stay with the freed block). The upper face remains stable while the maxilla floats, producing malocclusion with a mobile tooth-bearing segment.

steps.say: The middle line is outlining a pyramid with its tip at the nose. Nasal bones, the frontal process of the maxilla, lacrimal bones, the orbital floor, and the zygomaticomaxillary suture are all being crossed. The base is spanning the molar region while the apex is sitting at the nasal root.
steps.tx: **Le Fort II pyramidal fracture** (the central pyramid break) traverses **nasal bones** (the bridge framework), **frontal process of maxilla** (the lateral nasal wall strut), **lacrimal bones** (the tear duct housing), **orbital floor** (the eye socket base), and the **zygomaticomaxillary suture** (the cheek to maxilla seam). Apex at the nasal root, base across the molars.

rows: Pyramid apex at the nasal root

steps.say: The highest line is disconnecting the face from the skull. Frontonasal, frontomaxillary, and frontozygomatic sutures are all being crossed before the line is running back along both zygomatic arches. The entire facial skeleton is floating free of the cranial base.
steps.tx: **Le Fort III craniofacial dysjunction** (complete facial skeleton separation from the skull) traverses frontonasal, **frontomaxillary** (forehead to cheek seams), and **frontozygomatic** sutures plus the **zygomatic arches** (the cheek bars to the ear), freeing the face from the **cranial base** (the skull floor). Bilateral periorbital bruising with a mobile face marks this level.

steps.say: One broken strut is confirming every Le Fort level. Pterygoid plate fracture is pathognomonic and is appearing uniformly in all three classic patterns. Scan readers are checking the pterygoids first, and an intact pterygoid is ruling a Le Fort out.
steps.tx: **Pterygoid plate** fracture (a break of the thin vertical plates behind the maxilla) is **pathognomonic** (a sign proving the diagnosis) and uniformly present in all **three** classic Le Fort patterns. The plates anchor the posterior maxilla, so every transverse level snaps them. CT readers confirm the plates first; intact pterygoids exclude a Le Fort.

vis.alt: Skull with Le Fort fracture lines, orbital blowout CT, and lateral canthotomy for retrobulbar bleeding.
vis.caption: Le Fort patterns, blowout CT, and canthotomy for retrobulbar haematoma on one teaching panel. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: **Zygomaticomaxillary complex** **ZMC** fracture (the cheek **tetrapod** break) disrupts **four** articulations: the **frontozygomatic** suture (upper outer orbital rim), the **inferior orbital rim** (lower eye socket edge), the **zygomaticomaxillary buttress** (the cheek to upper-jaw pillar), and the **zygomatic arch** (the bar to the ear). A direct blow snaps all four struts as one unit.
steps.say: The cheek is breaking as a four-legged unit. Frontozygomatic suture, inferior orbital rim, zygomaticomaxillary buttress, and zygomatic arch are all giving way together under a direct blow. Four disrupted struts are defining the tetrapod pattern.

Three bedside findings are announcing a cheek fracture. Malar flattening is erasing the cheek prominence, trismus is following as the displaced arch is jamming the coronoid process, and the cheek and upper lip are going numb in infraorbital territory. This classic triad is meaning ZMC until proven otherwise.
steps.tx: The classic clinical **triad** (**three** bedside signs) of **ZMC** fractures (cheek complex breaks) combines **malar flattening** (lost cheek projection), **trismus** (locked jaw from arch impingement on the **coronoid** process) and **infraorbital nerve** numbness (cheek and upper-lip tingling). Three findings together localise the cheek complex before imaging confirms it.

rows: Displaced arch jams the coronoid process
Nerve bruised in the fractured canal

steps.say: A springy isolated arch is needing no plate, only a lift. The Gilles approach is passing through a small temporal hairline incision deep to the deep temporal fascia. An elevator is sliding beneath the depressed segment and is levering it back to contour.
steps.tx: **Gilles approach** (a closed temporal lift of the cheek arch) reduces isolated **zygomatic arch** fractures through a temporal hairline incision carried deep to deep **temporal fascia** (the tough sheet over the temporalis muscle), passing an elevator beneath the depressed arch. Displaced ZMC patterns instead need plating at the **frontozygomatic** suture and the **zygomaticomaxillary buttress** with low-profile **titanium miniplates** (thin bone plates hiding under cheek skin).
